_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the scoring weights: the top-level performanceComposite that blends the four supplier sub-scores, plus two risk composites (performanceRisk, which feeds the composite's risk_score component, and supplyRisk, the Kraljic Y-axis). Extracted from python/scores.py (composite + performanceRisk) and python/compute_analyses.py (supplyRisk) so every per-component weight is now an EXPLICIT normalized weight. For the risk composites each component's response curve is normalized to 0-100 in code and the WEIGHT here scales it; weight * 100 == the old point ceiling (country_distance 0.60->60, roster_concentration 0.40->40; supply_concentration 0.50->50, cost_premium 0.25->25, import_friction 0.25->25). performanceComposite is WEIGHTS ONLY: its components (quality_score/delivery_score/process_score/risk_score) are the EXISTING sub-scores computed by scores.py, not formula-defined, so they carry builtin:true and the future formula editor must never offer to edit their formula. Weights per composite MUST sum to 1.0. invertPolarity is a COMPUTE flag (=true applies the final 100-minus, performanceRisk higher=safer); performanceComposite uses invertPolarity=false because it is a weighted average of higher-is-better sub-scores (combine_score's clip is then a no-op). polarityLabel is the DISPLAY badge copy and is authoritative for the UI — never re-derive the badge from invertPolarity (they are different concerns: a compute flag vs display text). configuredIn links a built-in sub-score to the composite that PRODUCES it (risk_score -> performanceRisk); the two weight sets MULTIPLY, not add. ID CONVENTION (deliberate, not sloppiness): performanceComposite component ids ARE the scores.py column names (quality_score, delivery_score, process_score, risk_score) because these components are not formula-defined — they ARE those columns, and the id documenting exactly which column it reads is a feature, not a mapping layer that could drift. The risk composite ids (supply_concentration, cost_premium, ...) are unsuffixed because they are not columns. Consumed by python/risk_config.py (binding; reads weight/enabled/invertPolarity only) and lib/risk-model.ts (types + loader). VERSIONING (Stage 2): each composite carries its OWN `version` (bumped on save only when THAT composite's own components change); `schemaVersion` is the file-format version, separate. Fingerprints are DERIVED (never stored) over COMPUTE-AFFECTING fields only (weights, enabled, invertPolarity, derived dependsOn) — shortLabel/polarityLabel/label/definition/version/_comment are excluded, so a fingerprint change means the numbers changed. The printed report footer stamps the schema version + ALL per-composite versions + one whole-config fingerprint (a fingerprint is only comparable within one schemaVersion, which records the fingerprint's compute-affecting scope). Defaults live in config/risk-model.defaults.json (the reset-to-defaults target; keep in sync with the shipped weights here). Do NOT change weights without re-recording every affected baseline in the same change. LOOKUP TABLES (Stage A): the geographic + concentration lookups that used to be hardcoded in python/scores.py and python/compute_analyses.py now live in the top-level `lookupTables` block; a component references one by id via `lookupTable`. `concentration_curve` is SHARED by supplyRisk.supply_concentration AND performanceRisk.roster_concentration (one definition, two consumers -- editing it moves BOTH scores). country_distance and import_friction are deliberately SEPARATE tables (geography vs trade-agreement coverage). Each table carries key->value `rows` (with `members` = country codes for the geographic tables), an explicit REQUIRED `default`, and values validated to [0,100] at load. Read by python/risk_config.py (lookup_numeric / lookup_country) so scores.py and compute_analyses.py share ONE loader; table values are in the compute-affecting fingerprint scope (Stage 2), so editing the shared curve moves both consumers' compositeFingerprints. Adding lookup values to that scope EXPANDED the fingerprint's coverage, so schemaVersion moved 2.0.0->2.1.0 in the SAME change (commit fa7d75f): a fingerprint is only comparable within one schemaVersion, and a 2.0.0 vs 2.1.0 fingerprint differs at identical weights (RISK_MODEL_FINGERPRINT became e4db2d7e) WITHOUT any number changing. TABLE VERSIONING (Stage B): each lookup table carries its OWN `version`, bumped when THAT table is edited. A table edit moves its consumers' FINGERPRINTS but NOT their versions -- a shared table is no composite's own knob, so version stays per-editable-object and the fingerprint carries the transitive effect (same principle as composites). Table versions live in the config + the settings UI, NOT the report footer (which stays one line: schema + composite versions + whole-config fingerprint; the git-tracked config resolves a fingerprint to an exact historical state). `input` is STRUCTURE, never editable. count tables keep a contiguous 0..N key domain (a hole would silently fall through to `default`); country tables require DISJOINT members across rows (else the country->row match is order-dependent). Table defaults (the reset target) live in config/risk-model.defaults.json under `lookupTables`.

concentration_curve.label: Roster concentration curve
concentration_curve.definition: SHARED step curve on the number of OTHER suppliers in the same category across the full roster (active or not); fewer alternatives -> higher risk. Values are the normalized 0-100 axis (the old 0-50 points doubled: 50->100, 35->70, 22->44, 12->24, 5->10; the x2 that used to live in scores.concentration_0_100 is folded in here, bit-identical). Referenced by BOTH supplyRisk.supply_concentration AND performanceRisk.roster_concentration -- ONE definition, TWO consumers; editing it moves both scores, and is why the two risk scores correlate r=-0.852 (documented on the Methodology page). `input`=count: keyed by the integer other-in-category count; anything not listed (>=5, true abundance) falls through to `default` 0.

country_distance.label: Country distance tiers
country_distance.definition: Geographic supply-distance tier of the supplier's country (0 = domestic, 100 = far). Consumed by performanceRisk.country_distance. Deliberately SEPARATE from import_friction (geography, not trade blocs): India (IN) sits at 60 here (Asia-Pacific by geography) but at 100 on import_friction (outside RCEP since 2019) -- the divergence is intentional; do not unify. `input`=country: matched by ISO alpha-2 code (also full name for ID); any code in no row's `members` falls through to `default` 100.

import_friction.label: Import friction tiers
import_friction.definition: Indonesia trade-agreement coverage of the supplier's country (0 = domestic, 100 = no agreement). Consumed by supplyRisk.import_friction. Deliberately SEPARATE from country_distance (trade blocs, not geography): India is outside RCEP so lands at 100 here despite being Asia-Pacific (60) on distance. `input`=country: matched by ISO alpha-2 code (also IDN / full name for ID); any code in no row's `members` falls through to `default` 100.

components.label: Quality
components.definition: Existing quality sub-score: per-PO defect rate + complaint rate, each normalized 0-100 against fixed bounds, averaged. Computed by scores.py from transaction data; a built-in sub-score, not a formula-editable component.

components.label: Delivery
components.definition: Existing delivery sub-score: on-time-delivery % + average lead time, each normalized 0-100 against fixed bounds, averaged. Computed by scores.py from transaction data; a built-in sub-score, not a formula-editable component.

components.label: Process
components.definition: Existing process sub-score: three-way-match pass rate, normalized 0-100. Computed by scores.py from transaction data; a built-in sub-score, not a formula-editable component.

components.label: Risk
components.definition: The performanceRisk composite output (structural: country distance + roster concentration, inverted so higher=safer). A built-in sub-score, not a formula-editable component.

components.label: Country distance
components.definition: Geographic supply-distance tier of the supplier's country. 0-100 lookup {Indonesia:0, ASEAN:30, Asia-Pacific:60, other:100}.

components.label: Roster concentration
components.definition: Roster-based supply concentration (the SAME curve as supplyRisk.supply_concentration), on the 0-100 axis {0:100,1:70,2:44,3:24,4:10,>=5:0}.

components.label: Supply concentration
components.definition: Step curve on the number of OTHER suppliers in the same category across the full roster (active or not); fewer alternatives -> higher risk. Normalized curve {0:100,1:70,2:44,3:24,4:10,>=5:0}.

components.label: Cost premium
components.definition: Spend-weighted item-price premium vs the cross-supplier benchmark, over supplier x item pairs with >=2 POs where the item has >=2 suppliers. Normalized clip(premium*250, 0, 100); at/below market -> 0.

components.label: Import friction
components.definition: Indonesia trade-agreement coverage of the supplier's country. Normalized {domestic:0, AFTA:32, RCEP-non-ASEAN:64, other:100}.
